title: add-vpc-control-plane-provisioning-route53-peering-sgs-endpoints-terraform
author: Priya Nair
description: This PR adds Terraform automation to provision the VPC-based private control plane required for Redwood Private deployments. Motivation: customers running private control planes in AWS need a reproducible, auditable module that creates subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, VPC peering (cross-account), and Route53 delegated zones for service discovery. The previous docs included manual steps that were error-prone and inconsistent across accounts. This change implements a composable Terraform module, updates the installer Helm values reference, and provides an upgrade/rollback plan.
commits: feat(tf): new module aws/private-control-plane (subnets, endpoints, sgs, peering, route53)
chore(tf): add examples/ for single-account and cross-account peering topology
fix: export control_plane_endpoint and route53 zone id for installer
docs: add README + migration notes for existing VPCs
test(tf): terraform validate and integration smoke script
release_notes:
- Add terraform module infra/terraform/modules/aws/private-control-plane to automate subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, VPC peering and Route53 delegation.
- Installer now reads control_plane_endpoint and route53_zone_id outputs.
- Migration notes added for running against existing VPCs.

testing_notes: Unit: terraform validate + fmt + tflint run in GH Actions. Integration: smoke script (scripts/tf-integration/smoke-test.sh) provisions resources in a temporary account (cost-controlled), verifies endpoints, peering, and Route53 delegation, then tears down. Manual: installer deployed to a k8s cluster pointing at the newly-provisioned control plane and performed healthchecks (auth, reconciliation, metrics).
upgrade_plan: Backwards compatible: module can be used to provision new control planes. For existing manual setups, follow docs/private/vpc-control-plane-provisioning.md migration section. Key steps: 1) run terraform import for existing VPC/subnets/endpoints where possible, 2) apply module to create missing SGs and outputs, 3) update installer values to point at exported control_plane_endpoint and route53_zone_id, 4) perform rolling canary by pinning control plane version. A rollback can be done by updating installer values to previous endpoint and running terraform destroy selectively for resources created by the module.
notes_for_ops:
- If using cross-account peering, ensure peering accepter applies the provided example IAM policy.
- Route53 delegation requires creating NS records in customer account or creating a shared hosted zone; both supported by examples.
- Default SGs are restrictive; if customers need additional CIDR allowances, prefer security_group_rules input to the module.
changelog_entry: Added terraform module to automate VPC control plane provisioning (subnets, interface endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53). See docs/private/vpc-control-plane-provisioning.md for migration and examples.
